analysis:
Examined both BASE documentation excerpts (docs/provider/cli-reference.md:386–1226) and the bounded update patch. The patch adds offline predecessor rollback, confirmation, quarantine of the replaced release, and drain/update-lease/watchdog integration (HEAD:743–747, 751 onward). These statements alone do not establish a security regression: offline restoration is not serving authorization, and existing watchdog rollback is already modeled by T-043. Surrounding documentation preserves issuer-bound logout and process-exit locking (BASE:629–651; A-008/T-053), fail-closed model verification and bounded Autopilot consent (BASE:882–913; T-012/T-027), and the TLS-only installer trust limitation (BASE:1051–1058; TB-013/T-061). No supplied change establishes altered prompt encryption, cache isolation, billing, attestation, or privileged fan controls; this is documentation coverage, not verification of those implementations.
Integration must inspect provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/UpdateRollback.swift and the changed updater/watchdog paths to verify predecessor identity/integrity, prompt-to-activation generation checks, lifecycle lease ownership, recovery after partial swaps, and preservation of explicit stopped state. Confirm that rollback does not bypass current build qualification/revocation or connection-bound authorization (A-017, T-054, T-053), and reconcile quarantine semantics with automatic recovery (T-043). Runtime source and the remainder of the truncated rollback documentation are absent here; these material rollback contracts remain unverified rather than findings.
